---
title: "Vue SDK"
description: "@seamless-auth/vue adds Seamless Auth to a Vue 3.5 application: a plugin and useSeamlessAuth() composable, vue-router guards, and optional sign-in screens."
sidebar:
  order: 4.8
---

`@seamless-auth/vue` is the official Vue integration for Seamless Auth. It gives a Vue application
the same session state, auth actions, and optional sign-in screens the [React SDK](/build/react-sdk)
gives a React app, in Vue's own idioms: a plugin, a `useSeamlessAuth()` composable that returns
read-only refs, and `vue-router` guards.

It is a thin binding over `@seamless-auth/client`, the framework-free core the React, React Native,
and [Angular](/build/angular-sdk) SDKs also build on, so sign-in behaves the same in every binding.
The Vue screens keep the React screens' accessible names, and `seamless verify` runs the same browser
specs against both.

---

## How It Fits

```txt
Vue app (browser)
  -> your backend's /auth adapter routes, with signed httpOnly cookies
  -> Seamless Auth API
```

The browser model is the same as React's: the [server adapter](/build/server-sdks) keeps the auth
API's tokens and the browser holds only `httpOnly` cookies on your domain. The Vue SDK has no bearer
mode. Its configuration has no transport option, so no token can reach page scripts, and nothing it
writes to browser storage is a credential. See
[Cookie, Session, And Token Reference](/reference/cookies-sessions-tokens).

---

## Requirements

- Vue 3.5 or later
- `vue-router` 4.4 or later (5 included) for the guards and screens in `@seamless-auth/vue/router`.
  The root entry does not need it
- A backend mounting the Seamless Auth adapter routes at `/auth`, for example `@seamless-auth/express`

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install @seamless-auth/vue
```

`@seamless-auth/client` comes with it.

---

## Configure The Application

```ts
// main.ts
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router'
import { createSeamlessAuth } from '@seamless-auth/vue'
import { authGuard, createSeamlessAuthRoutes, guestGuard } from '@seamless-auth/vue/router'

import App from './App.vue'
import HomePage from './HomePage.vue'

const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/', component: HomePage, beforeEnter: authGuard },
    ...createSeamlessAuthRoutes(),
  ],
})

createApp(App)
  .use(router)
  .use(createSeamlessAuth({ apiHost: 'https://app.example.com' }))
  .mount('#app')
```

`apiHost` is the origin your backend serves `/auth` on. Each application the plugin is installed in
gets its own session, and the session is read as soon as the application starts in the browser.

| Option                     | Default          | Purpose                                                              |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiHost`                  | required         | Origin of the server adapter                                         |
| `basePath`                 | `/auth`          | Where the adapter is mounted on `apiHost`                            |
| `magicLinkRedirectUri`     | the deployment's | Where an emailed magic link lands                                    |
| `autoDetectPreviousSignIn` | `true`           | Open the login screen on Sign In for a browser that signed in before |
| `initialSession`           | none             | A session your server already resolved, for server rendering         |
| `ports`                    | browser          | `passkeys` and `oauthRedirect` ports                                 |
| `fetch`                    | global `fetch`   | The fetch auth requests go through                                   |
| `trustedOrigins`           | none             | Other origins of yours that may receive the session cookies          |
| `injectStyles`             | `true`           | Whether the built-in screens add their stylesheet to the page        |
| `cspNonce`                 | none             | A CSP nonce for that stylesheet                                      |
| `signedInPath`             | `/`              | Where the built-in screens go after sign-in                          |
| `loginPath`                | `/login`         | Where `requireAuth` sends someone who is signed out                  |

---

## Guards

| Guard                                   | Admits                                    | Otherwise                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `authGuard` / `requireAuth(options?)`   | A signed-in user, with `roles` when given | `redirectTo` (default `loginPath`). A missing role goes to `forbiddenRedirectTo`, or is refused |
| `guestGuard` / `requireGuest(options?)` | Someone signed out                        | `redirectTo` (default `signedInPath`)                                                          |

Use them as `beforeEnter`, or call one from `router.beforeEach`. They wait for the session to be read
before deciding, so reloading a protected page does not bounce a signed-in user to the login screen.

`roles` uses the same matching as the auth API, scoped roles such as `org:admin` included. A guard
decides what to render; it is not access control. Your backend still checks every request with
`requireAuth`. See [Secure Routes](/build/secure-routes).

Put `guestGuard` only on the screens that start a sign-in (`login`, `passkey-login`,
`magic-link-sent`). A user can already have a session when `register-passkey`, `oauth/callback`, or
`verify-magiclink` renders, and the guard would send them on before they finish.

---

## The `useSeamlessAuth()` Composable

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router'
import { useSeamlessAuth } from '@seamless-auth/vue'

const auth = useSeamlessAuth()
const router = useRouter()

async function signOut() {
  await auth.logout()
  await router.push('/login')
}
</script>

<template>
  <span v-if="auth.user.value">{{ auth.user.value.email }}</span>
  <button v-if="auth.isAuthenticated.value" type="button" @click="signOut">Logout</button>
</template>
```

- **Read-only refs:** `state`, `user`, `isAuthenticated`, `loading`, `credentials`, `organizations`,
  `activeOrganization`, `stepUpStatus`, `hasSignedInBefore`, plus `loginMethods`,
  `loginMethodsLoading`, `passkeySupported`, and `passkeySupportLoading`.
- **Actions:** `login`, `handlePasskeyLogin`, `registerPasskey`, `refreshSession`, `logout`,
  `logoutAllSessions`, `deleteUser`, `updateCredential`, `deleteCredential`, `switchOrganization`,
  `listOAuthProviders`, `startOAuthLogin`, `finishOAuthLogin`, `refreshStepUpStatus`,
  `verifyStepUpWithPasskey`, `verifyStepUpWithPasskeyPrf`, and `verifyStepUpWithTotp`.
- **Also:** `hasRole`, `hasScopedRole`, `markSignedIn`, `whenSettled()`, `loadLoginMethods()` and
  `checkPasskeySupport()` (each read once and cached), `authorizedFetch`, `client` (the headless
  client for OTP, magic link, organization, and TOTP calls), and `ports`.

Every request action resolves to a `SeamlessAuthResult<T>`, `{ data, error }`, and does not throw
for an HTTP or network failure, the same convention as the React SDK. `authorizedFetch` sends the
session only to `apiHost` and `trustedOrigins`; see
[Calling Your Own API](/build/react-sdk#calling-your-own-api).

---

## Built-In Screens

`createSeamlessAuthRoutes({ basePath? })` returns the screens as named routes
(`seamless-auth-login` and so on) to spread into your router. They reach each other by name, so any
`basePath` works. There is no catch-all among them, so they never swallow your own unknown paths.

| Path               | Component           | Purpose                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `login`            | `SaLogin`           | Sign in with an email or phone number, or create an account |
| `passkey-login`    | `SaPasskeyLogin`    | Sign in with a passkey alone                                |
| `verify-email-otp` | `SaVerifyOtp`       | Check an email code                                         |
| `verify-phone-otp` | `SaVerifyOtp`       | Check a text message code                                   |
| `magic-link-sent`  | `SaMagicLinkSent`   | Wait for an emailed link to be used                         |
| `verify-magiclink` | `SaVerifyMagicLink` | Where the emailed link lands. The auth API builds this URL  |
| `oauth/callback`   | `SaOAuthCallback`   | The OAuth redirect URI to register with your providers      |
| `register-passkey` | `SaRegisterPasskey` | Offer passkey enrolment after sign-up                       |

The building blocks are exported too: `SaOtpInput` (bind it with `v-model`), `SaFallbackOptions`,
`SaOAuthProviderButtons`, `SaAuthLayout`, `authRoutePaths`, `authRouteName`, and
`useAuthNavigation`.

The magic link and OAuth callback screens remove the token or code from the address bar once they
have read it. Serve those routes with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (or `same-origin`) so the
secret does not leave in a `Referer` before then.

### Styling

The screens render inside `.sa-auth` with plain `.sa-*` classes. The first screen to mount adds the
stylesheet to the top of `<head>`, so your own styles override it. Colors come from the same
`--seamless-*` custom properties the React and Angular screens read, so one theme covers every
binding:

```css
:root {
  --seamless-accent: #1f3a34;
  --seamless-accent-hover: #16302b;
  --seamless-surface: #f7f5f0;
  --seamless-surface-raised: #ffffff;
  --seamless-text: #1a1a1a;
  --seamless-text-muted: #4b5563;
}
```

Under a Content Security Policy, pass `cspNonce`, or set `injectStyles: false` and link
`@seamless-auth/vue/seamless-auth.css` yourself. The full token list is in the
[`@seamless-auth/react` README](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-react/tree/main/packages/react#theming-the-built-in-ui).

## Custom Screens

Every built-in screen is a thin view over a flow in `@seamless-auth/client`: `beginSignIn`,
`registerWithEmail`, `requestOtp` and `verifyOtp`, `watchMagicLink` and `finishMagicLinkSignIn`,
`startOAuthSignIn` and `completeOAuthCallback`, `enrollPasskey`, plus helpers such as
`loadLoginMethods`, `fallbackSignInOptions`, and `safeReturnPath`. A custom screen calls the same
flows, passing the session as its actions:

```ts
import { beginSignIn } from '@seamless-auth/client'

const step = await beginSignIn(auth, {
  identifier: email.value,
  passkeySupported: await auth.checkPasskeySupport(),
  configuredMethods: await auth.loadLoginMethods(),
})

if (step.kind === 'signed_in') await router.push('/')
if (step.kind === 'choose_method') showOtherMethods(step.loginMethods)
if (step.kind === 'error') showError(step.message)
```

[How To Build Your Own Auth UI](/build/custom-auth-ui) walks through the flows in order. Its
examples use React hooks, but the client calls are the same.

---

## Server Rendering

On the server the session is not read and no screen starts a request: a server render has none of the
browser's cookies, and a magic link or OAuth code is single use. `loading` stays true unless you pass
`initialSession`. Without it, `requireAuth` treats the request as signed out and redirects to
`loginPath`, so a protected page's data never renders into a response for someone the server could
not identify; the browser decides again when the application boots.

To render a known session on the first paint, resolve it on your server through your adapter and pass
it as `initialSession`, building the plugin's config per request so one visitor's session is never
another's. Do not forward the browser's cookies to the adapter's `/auth/users/me` from a server.
